clue_checks.clue: My older brother was a tiller of the ground.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 4:2 says Abel was born after Cain ('again bare his brother Abel') and that Cain was a tiller of the ground. This early clue could also fit Seth, but later clues single out Abel.

clue_checks.clue: I was a keeper of sheep.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 4:2 states 'Abel was a keeper of sheep.'

clue_checks.clue: The LORD had respect unto my offering from the firstlings of my flock.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 4:4 says Abel brought of the firstlings of his flock and that the LORD had respect unto Abel and to his offering.

clue_checks.clue: My brother rose up against me in the field.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 4:8 says that when they were in the field, Cain rose up against Abel his brother.

clue_checks.clue: I was an Egyptian handmaid of Sarai.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 16:1 says Sarai had a handmaid, an Egyptian, named Hagar.

clue_checks.clue: I fled into the wilderness, and an angel found me by a fountain of water.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 16:6-7 says she fled from Sarai and the angel of the LORD found her by a fountain of water in the wilderness.

clue_checks.clue: I called the LORD who spoke to me, Thou God seest me.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 16:13 quotes this directly.

clue_checks.clue: My son was Ishmael.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 16:15 says Hagar bare Abram a son, whom Abram named Ishmael.

clue_checks.clue: My eyes are described as tender.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 29:17 states 'Leah was tender eyed.'

clue_checks.clue: My father gave me to Jacob in place of my younger sister.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 29:23-26 says Laban brought Leah to Jacob, who had served for Rachel. Laban explains that the younger is not given before the firstborn.

clue_checks.clue: I was the mother of Reuben, Levi and Judah.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 29:32-35 records that Leah bore Reuben, Simeon, Levi and Judah.

clue_checks.clue: My younger sister was Rachel.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 29:16 names Leah as the elder and Rachel as the younger daughter of Laban.

clue_checks.clue: My mother was an Egyptian handmaid.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 16:1 identifies Hagar as Sarai's Egyptian handmaid. Hagar is Ishmael's mother (Gen 16:15).

clue_checks.clue: An angel told my mother my name before I was born.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 16:11: the angel of the LORD tells the pregnant Hagar to call her son Ishmael. Isaac's name was told to his father, not his mother (Gen 17:19), so this clue does not fit Isaac.

clue_checks.clue: My name was given because the LORD had heard my mother's affliction.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 16:11 explicitly gives this reason for the name Ishmael.

clue_checks.clue: My father was Abraham, but I was not the son of the promise.
clue_checks.reason: Galatians 4:22-23 contrasts Abraham's son by the bondwoman, born after the flesh, with the son by promise. In context the bondwoman's son is Ishmael.

clue_checks.clue: I was the youngest son of Jacob.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 42:13 says the youngest brother is with their father but does not name him. Context (Genesis 42:4) makes clear this is Benjamin, so the clue fits but the cited verse alone does not name him.

clue_checks.clue: My mother died as I was born, and she called me Benoni.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 35:18 says Rachel named him Ben-oni as her soul was departing, for she died. Verses 16–17 place this at the birth.

clue_checks.clue: Joseph's silver cup was found in my sack.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 44:12 says the cup was found in Benjamin's sack. Genesis 44:2 identifies it as Joseph's silver cup, so this is minor paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: My full brother was Joseph.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 35:24 lists Joseph and Benjamin as the sons of Rachel, so they were full brothers.

clue_checks.clue: I was the brother of Rebekah.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 24:29 says directly that Rebekah had a brother named Laban.

clue_checks.clue: My nephew served me seven years for my younger daughter.
clue_checks.reason: The passage confirms that Jacob served Laban seven years for Rachel, 'thy younger daughter.' It does not call Jacob his nephew. That kinship is stated elsewhere ('Laban his mother's brother,' Genesis 29:10), so the clue is accurate but goes beyond the cited text.

clue_checks.clue: On the wedding night I gave him my older daughter instead.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 29:23 says Laban brought Leah to Jacob in the evening. That she was the elder comes from 29:16, and the wedding setting comes from 29:22. The clue is accurate but draws slightly on surrounding verses.

clue_checks.clue: My daughters were Leah and Rachel.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 29:16 names Laban's two daughters as Leah (elder) and Rachel (younger).

clue_checks.clue: I was Jacob's firstborn son.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 35:23 explicitly calls Reuben 'Jacob's firstborn.'

clue_checks.clue: I found mandrakes in the field and brought them to my mother.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 30:14 says Reuben found mandrakes in the field and brought them to his mother Leah.

clue_checks.clue: I persuaded my brothers to cast Joseph into a pit instead of killing him.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 37:21-22 has Reuben say 'Let us not kill him... cast him into this pit.' 'Persuaded' is a fair paraphrase, since verse 24 confirms they cast him in.

clue_checks.clue: I planned to rescue Joseph and bring him back to our father.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 37:22 gives his purpose: 'that he might rid him out of their hands, to deliver him to his father again.'

clue_checks.clue: I was the fourth son of Leah.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 29:35 names Judah, but the verse alone does not name Leah or say 'fourth'. Those details come from the context in 29:31-34, where Leah bears Reuben, Simeon and Levi first. The clue is accurate.

clue_checks.clue: I said, let us sell our brother rather than kill him.
clue_checks.reason: Judah asks what profit there is in slaying their brother and proposes selling him to the Ishmeelites.

clue_checks.clue: In Egypt I offered to stay as a bondman in place of my youngest brother.
clue_checks.reason: The verse records the offer to abide as a bondman instead of 'the lad'. The speaker being Judah (44:18) and the lad being Benjamin, the youngest, come from context. The clue is accurate.

clue_checks.clue: Jacob said the sceptre would not depart from me.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 49:10 explicitly says the sceptre shall not depart from Judah.

clue_checks.clue: The prophetess Deborah called me to fight.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 4:6 says Deborah sent and called Barak and relayed the LORD's command to take ten thousand men toward mount Tabor.

clue_checks.clue: I would not go to battle unless Deborah went with me.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 4:8 records Barak's condition almost word for word.

clue_checks.clue: I led ten thousand men down from mount Tabor.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 4:14: 'So Barak went down from mount Tabor, and ten thousand men after him.'

clue_checks.clue: I fought against Sisera, captain of Jabin's army.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 4:7 names Sisera as captain of Jabin's army, but only as God's promise to deliver him into Barak's hand. The actual battle is in Judges 4:15-16. The clue is accurate, but this passage does not itself record the fighting.

clue_checks.clue: I was a Gileadite and a mighty man of valour.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 11:1 calls Jephthah 'the Gileadite' and 'a mighty man of valour.' Gideon is also called a mighty man of valour (Judges 6:12), but he was not a Gileadite.

clue_checks.clue: My brothers drove me out, and I lived in the land of Tob.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 11:2-3: his father's wife's sons thrust him out, and he 'fled from his brethren, and dwelt in the land of Tob.' 'Brothers' is a fair paraphrase of these half-brothers.

clue_checks.clue: I made a vow to the LORD before fighting the children of Ammon.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 11:30-31 records Jephthah's vow before the Ammonites were delivered into his hands.

clue_checks.clue: My daughter came out to meet me with timbrels and dances.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 11:34 states this directly.

clue_checks.clue: I took a Babylonish garment, silver and a wedge of gold from Jericho.
clue_checks.reason: Joshua 7:21 confirms the garment, silver and wedge of gold were taken 'among the spoils', but the verse does not name Jericho. That detail comes from the surrounding context (Joshua 6–7), so it is accurate but not in the cited text.

clue_checks.clue: I hid them in the earth in the middle of my tent.
clue_checks.reason: Joshua 7:21 says 'they are hid in the earth in the midst of my tent.'

clue_checks.clue: Because of my sin, Israel was defeated at Ai.
clue_checks.reason: Joshua 7:4-5 describes the defeat at Ai but does not link it to Achan's sin. The causal link is stated in Joshua 7:1 and 7:11-12.

clue_checks.clue: I was the son of Carmi, of the tribe of Judah.
clue_checks.reason: Joshua 7:1 names 'Achan, the son of Carmi... of the tribe of Judah.'

clue_checks.clue: The LORD raised me up as a deliverer of Israel; I was a Benjamite.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 3:15 says the LORD raised up a deliverer, Ehud the son of Gera, a Benjamite. Being a Benjamite rules out Othniel, who was of Kenaz and Judah.

clue_checks.clue: I was left-handed.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 3:15 calls Ehud 'a man lefthanded.'

clue_checks.clue: I made a dagger with two edges, a cubit long.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 3:16 says Ehud 'made him a dagger which had two edges, of a cubit length.'

clue_checks.clue: I killed Eglon, the king of Moab.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 3:21 shows Ehud thrusting the dagger into 'his belly', but it does not name Eglon or state that he died. Eglon is identified in context (3:17-20), and his death appears in 3:25 ('their lord was fallen down dead'). The proposed verse alone does not fully state the claim.

clue_checks.clue: My husband Elimelech and I moved to Moab during a famine.
clue_checks.reason: Ruth 1:1-2 says that during a famine Elimelech went to sojourn in Moab with his wife Naomi and their two sons.

clue_checks.clue: My husband and both my sons died in Moab.
clue_checks.reason: Ruth 1:3-5 records the deaths of Elimelech and then of Mahlon and Chilion while the family dwelled in Moab. It says 'the woman was left of her two sons and her husband.'

clue_checks.clue: I asked to be called Mara, because the Almighty had dealt very bitterly with me.
clue_checks.reason: Ruth 1:20 quotes Naomi almost word for word: 'Call me not Naomi, call me Mara: for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me.'

clue_checks.clue: My daughter-in-law Ruth would not leave me.
clue_checks.reason: In Ruth 1:16 Ruth pledges not to leave the person she is addressing. The context (1:4, 1:15) identifies that person as Naomi, her mother-in-law, so the clue is a fair paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: I was the son of Jonathan.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 4:4 says Jonathan, Saul's son, had a son whose name was Mephibosheth.

clue_checks.clue: I became lame when my nurse fled with me and I fell.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 4:4 says his nurse took him up and fled, and as she hurried he fell and became lame.

clue_checks.clue: King David restored to me all the land of Saul.
clue_checks.reason: In 2 Samuel 9:7 David says he 'will restore thee all the land of Saul thy father.' 2 Samuel 9:9 confirms the grant was carried out.

clue_checks.clue: I ate continually at the king's table.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 9:13 says Mephibosheth 'did eat continually at the king's table.'

clue_checks.clue: I was the captain of King David's army.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 8:16 says Joab the son of Zeruiah 'was over the host' in David's administration.

clue_checks.clue: My mother was Zeruiah.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 2:18 names Joab among the 'three sons of Zeruiah'. Scripture consistently identifies the brothers by Zeruiah, David's sister (1 Chronicles 2:16).

clue_checks.clue: I killed Abner at the gate of Hebron.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 3:27 says Joab took Abner aside 'in the gate' at Hebron and smote him so that he died.

clue_checks.clue: I thrust three darts through Absalom's heart as he hung in an oak.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 18:14 says Joab thrust three darts through Absalom's heart while he was alive 'in the midst of the oak'. That Absalom was hanging comes from 18:9-10, which is consistent with the clue.

clue_checks.clue: I was a Hittite and one of David's mighty men.
clue_checks.reason: The quoted verse confirms 'Uriah the Hittite' as the last name in the list. The 'mighty men' part comes from the list's heading in 2 Samuel 23:8 ('the names of the mighty men whom David had'), not from the quoted text itself. Accurate in context.

clue_checks.clue: I would not go down to my house while the ark and the army stayed in tents.
clue_checks.reason: In 2 Samuel 11:11 Uriah says the ark, Israel and Judah abide in tents, and asks 'shall I then go into mine house… I will not do this thing.' The phrase 'went not down to his house' appears in 11:9-10.

clue_checks.clue: I carried a letter to Joab that arranged my own death.
clue_checks.reason: David sent the letter 'by the hand of Uriah', and it ordered him set in the forefront of the hottest battle 'that he may be smitten, and die' (2 Samuel 11:14-15).

clue_checks.clue: My wife was Bathsheba.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 11:3 calls Bath-sheba 'the wife of Uriah the Hittite.'

clue_checks.clue: I was a servant of Solomon, from the tribe of Ephraim.
clue_checks.reason: The verse calls Jeroboam 'Solomon's servant' and 'an Ephrathite of Zereda.' In this context 'Ephrathite' denotes an Ephraimite, but the KJV wording does not say 'tribe of Ephraim' explicitly. This is a minor interpretive paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: The prophet Ahijah tore a new garment into twelve pieces and gave me ten.
clue_checks.reason: Ahijah rent the new garment in twelve pieces and told Jeroboam, 'Take thee ten pieces' (1 Kings 11:30-31).

clue_checks.clue: I became king over the ten northern tribes.
clue_checks.reason: Israel made Jeroboam king, and only Judah followed the house of David. Together with the promise of ten tribes in 11:31, 'ten northern tribes' is a fair paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: I set up calves of gold in Beth-el and in Dan.
clue_checks.reason: He made two calves of gold, setting one in Beth-el and the other in Dan.

clue_checks.clue: I was the servant of the prophet Elisha.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 4:12 calls Gehazi 'his servant,' and in context 'he' is Elisha (see 4:8-11). 2 Kings 5:20 also explicitly calls him 'the servant of Elisha.'

clue_checks.clue: I told my master that the Shunammite woman had no child.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 4:14: 'Gehazi answered, Verily she hath no child, and her husband is old.'

clue_checks.clue: I ran after Naaman and took silver and garments from him.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 5:20-23 shows Gehazi running after Naaman and asking for silver and garments, which Naaman then gives. Verse 24 confirms that Gehazi took them; this is minor paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: The leprosy of Naaman clung to me.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 5:27: 'The leprosy therefore of Naaman shall cleave unto thee... he went out from his presence a leper as white as snow,' spoken to Gehazi in context.

clue_checks.clue: I was the son of Solomon.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 11:43 states that Rehoboam, Solomon's son, reigned in his stead.

clue_checks.clue: I rejected the counsel of the old men and followed the young men.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 12:8 says he forsook the old men's counsel and consulted the young men. In context the 'he' is Rehoboam, and 12:14 confirms he acted on their counsel. This is a fair paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: I told the people, my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 12:14 matches nearly verbatim.

clue_checks.clue: The ten tribes of Israel rebelled against me.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 12:19 says 'Israel rebelled against the house of David', not 'ten tribes' or 'against me' personally. The ten-tribe detail comes from 1 Kings 11:31-35, and in context 12:16-18 shows the rebellion was against Rehoboam. Accurate in substance, but the wording goes beyond the cited verse.

clue_checks.clue: A young prophet anointed me king over Israel.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 9:4-6 says the young man, the prophet, poured oil on Jehu's head and said, 'I have anointed thee king... even over Israel.'

clue_checks.clue: The watchman knew me because I drove furiously.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 9:20 says the watchman recognized the driving as that of Jehu the son of Nimshi, 'for he driveth furiously.'

clue_checks.clue: I had Jezebel thrown down from a window.
clue_checks.reason: The command 'Throw her down' in 9:33 is Jehu's. However, the quoted verse names neither Jehu nor the window; those details come from 9:30-32. The clue is accurate in context, but the excerpt alone does not fully show it.

clue_checks.clue: I destroyed the worship of Baal out of Israel.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 10:28: 'Thus Jehu destroyed Baal out of Israel.' 'Worship of Baal' is an acceptable paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: I was king of Babylon.
clue_checks.reason: Daniel 1:1 names 'Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon.' Belshazzar was also king of Babylon, but an early clue may fit another option.

clue_checks.clue: I dreamed of a great image with a head of gold.
clue_checks.reason: Daniel 2:31-32 describes the great image with a head of fine gold seen by 'O king,' but the quoted verses do not name the king. Context (Daniel 2:1, 2:28) identifies him as Nebuchadnezzar, so the clue is accurate but not fully supported by the excerpt alone.

clue_checks.clue: I set up a golden image and commanded everyone to worship it.
clue_checks.reason: Daniel 3:1-5 says Nebuchadnezzar made and set up an image of gold. A herald, speaking on the king's behalf, commanded all people, nations and languages to fall down and worship it.

clue_checks.clue: I ate grass as oxen until I knew that the most High rules.
clue_checks.reason: Daniel 4:32 states the decree that he would eat grass as oxen 'until thou know that the most High ruleth.' Daniel 4:33 records this fulfilled upon Nebuchadnezzar.

clue_checks.clue: I was a king of the Chaldeans in Babylon.
clue_checks.reason: Daniel 5:30 calls Belshazzar 'the king of the Chaldeans'. 'In Babylon' is not in this verse, though it is clear from the chapter (e.g., Daniel 5:7). The clue alone also fits Nebuchadnezzar, which is acceptable for an early clue.

clue_checks.clue: I drank wine from the golden vessels taken from the temple in Jerusalem.
clue_checks.reason: Daniel 5:3 says the king drank from the golden vessels taken from the temple at Jerusalem. Daniel 5:2 identifies that king as Belshazzar, and the wine is mentioned in 5:2 and 5:4.

clue_checks.clue: The fingers of a man's hand wrote on the wall of my palace.
clue_checks.reason: Daniel 5:5 says the fingers of a man's hand wrote upon the plaister of the wall of the king's palace.

clue_checks.clue: I was slain that same night.
clue_checks.reason: Daniel 5:30 says 'In that night was Belshazzar the king of the Chaldeans slain.'

clue_checks.clue: I was king of Persia.
clue_checks.reason: Ezra 1:1 calls him 'Cyrus king of Persia.' Darius and Artaxerxes also fit this clue, but that is acceptable for an early clue.

clue_checks.clue: The LORD stirred up my spirit to make a proclamation.
clue_checks.reason: Ezra 1:1 says 'the LORD stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, that he made a proclamation.'

clue_checks.clue: I declared that a house should be built for the LORD at Jerusalem.
clue_checks.reason: Ezra 1:2-3 records Cyrus proclaiming that the LORD charged him to build a house at Jerusalem, and inviting the people to go up and build it.

clue_checks.clue: Isaiah calls me the LORD's anointed.
clue_checks.reason: Isaiah 45:1 reads 'Thus saith the LORD to his anointed, to Cyrus.'

clue_checks.clue: I was a blind beggar sitting by the highway near Jericho.
clue_checks.reason: Mark 10:46 says blind Bartimaeus sat by the highway side begging as Jesus went out of Jericho.

clue_checks.clue: I cried out, Jesus, thou son of David, have mercy on me.
clue_checks.reason: Mark 10:47 records this cry nearly verbatim.

clue_checks.clue: When many told me to be quiet, I cried all the more.
clue_checks.reason: Mark 10:48: many charged him to hold his peace, but he cried the more a great deal.

clue_checks.clue: I cast away my garment, came to Jesus and received my sight.
clue_checks.reason: Mark 10:50-52 records him casting away his garment, coming to Jesus, and immediately receiving his sight.

clue_checks.clue: I was a Jew who sat in the king's gate in Shushan.
clue_checks.reason: Esther 2:5 confirms Mordecai was a Jew in Shushan the palace. It does not say he sat in the king's gate; that detail comes from Esther 2:19 and 2:21. The clue is accurate overall but goes beyond the cited verse.

clue_checks.clue: I reported a plot by two chamberlains to kill the king.
clue_checks.reason: Esther 2:21-22 says Bigthan and Teresh sought to lay hand on the king. Mordecai told Esther, who certified the king in Mordecai's name.

clue_checks.clue: I would not bow down to Haman.
clue_checks.reason: Esther 3:2 says Mordecai bowed not, nor did him reverence.

clue_checks.clue: I raised my cousin Esther as my own daughter.
clue_checks.reason: Esther 2:7 calls Esther his uncle's daughter, which makes her his cousin, and says he took her for his own daughter.

clue_checks.clue: My father was Zebedee.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 4:21 names 'James the son of Zebedee' and says they were 'with Zebedee their father.'

clue_checks.clue: I was mending nets in a ship when Jesus called me.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 4:21 says James and John were 'in a ship with Zebedee their father, mending their nets; and he called them.' Peter and Andrew were casting a net (4:18), not mending.

clue_checks.clue: Jesus called my brother and me Boanerges, the sons of thunder.
clue_checks.reason: Mark 3:17 says Jesus surnamed James and John 'Boanerges, which is, The sons of thunder.'

clue_checks.clue: King Herod killed me with the sword.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 12:1-2 says 'Herod the king... killed James the brother of John with the sword.'

clue_checks.clue: King Ahasuerus set me above all the princes.
clue_checks.reason: Esther 3:1 says Ahasuerus promoted Haman and set his seat above all the princes that were with him.

clue_checks.clue: I was full of wrath because a Jew would not bow to me.
clue_checks.reason: Esther 3:5 says Haman was full of wrath when Mordecai bowed not. Mordecai is identified as a Jew in the context (Esther 2:5; 3:4), so this is a fair paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: Pur, that is, the lot, was cast before me to choose a day to destroy the Jews.
clue_checks.reason: Esther 9:24 confirms that Haman cast Pur, that is, the lot, to consume and destroy the Jews. However, the wording 'before me' and 'to choose a day' comes from Esther 3:7 ('they cast Pur, that is, the lot, before Haman from day to day'), not from 9:24. Esther 3:7 would be the more precise reference.

clue_checks.clue: I was hanged on the gallows I had prepared for another man.
clue_checks.reason: Esther 7:10 says they hanged Haman on the gallows he had prepared for Mordecai.

clue_checks.clue: I was queen to King Ahasuerus.
clue_checks.reason: Esther 1:9 calls her 'Vashti the queen' in the royal house of king Ahasuerus. Esther was also his queen, but this is an early clue and later clues narrow it to Vashti.

clue_checks.clue: I made a feast for the women in the royal house.
clue_checks.reason: Esther 1:9 says this directly: 'Vashti the queen made a feast for the women in the royal house.'

clue_checks.clue: I refused to come when the king sent his chamberlains for me.
clue_checks.reason: Esther 1:12 says 'the queen Vashti refused to come at the king's commandment by his chamberlains.'

clue_checks.clue: My royal estate was given to another who was better than I.
clue_checks.reason: Esther 1:19 is only Memucan's proposal ('let the king give her royal estate unto another that is better than she'). The cited verse does not record the estate actually being given. The king adopts the advice in 1:21, and Esther is made queen instead of Vashti in 2:17.

clue_checks.clue: My sister was Martha and my brother was Lazarus.
clue_checks.reason: John 11:1-2 names Bethany as the town of Mary and her sister Martha, and says it was Mary whose brother Lazarus was sick.

clue_checks.clue: I sat at Jesus' feet and heard his word.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 10:39 says Martha's sister Mary sat at Jesus' feet and heard his word. John 11 ties this Martha-and-Mary household to Bethany.

clue_checks.clue: Jesus said I had chosen that good part.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 10:42 records Jesus saying that Mary hath chosen that good part.

clue_checks.clue: I anointed Jesus' feet with costly spikenard and wiped them with my hair.
clue_checks.reason: John 12:3 matches this nearly word for word. The context (John 12:1-2: Bethany, Lazarus, Martha serving) identifies this Mary as Mary of Bethany.

clue_checks.clue: I was a ruler of the synagogue.
clue_checks.reason: Mark 5:22 calls Jairus 'one of the rulers of the synagogue.' Nicodemus was 'a ruler of the Jews' (John 3:1), not of a synagogue, so this clue does not clearly fit another option.

clue_checks.clue: I fell at Jesus' feet and begged him to come to my house.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 8:41 says he 'fell down at Jesus' feet, and besought him that he would come into his house.'

clue_checks.clue: My little daughter lay at the point of death.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 8:42 says his only daughter, about twelve, 'lay a dying,' which supports the substance. The wording 'little daughter … at the point of death' comes from Mark 5:23, not from the cited verse.

clue_checks.clue: Jesus took her by the hand and said, Talitha cumi.
clue_checks.reason: Mark 5:41 says he took the damsel by the hand and said 'Talitha cumi.' The context (Mark 5:35-40) identifies her as Jairus's daughter.

clue_checks.clue: I was passing by, coming out of the country.
clue_checks.reason: Mark 15:21 says Simon 'passed by, coming out of the country.'

clue_checks.clue: I was compelled to bear a cross.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 27:32 says 'him they compelled to bear his cross.'

clue_checks.clue: The cross I carried was the cross of Jesus.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 23:26 says they 'led him [Jesus] away' and laid the cross on Simon 'that he might bear it after Jesus.' Matthew and Mark both call it 'his cross,' meaning Jesus' cross.

clue_checks.clue: I came from Cyrene and was the father of Alexander and Rufus.
clue_checks.reason: Mark 15:21 calls him 'a Cyrenian' and 'the father of Alexander and Rufus.' Saying he came from Cyrene is a fair paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: I was an honourable counsellor who waited for the kingdom of God.
clue_checks.reason: Mark 15:43 calls Joseph of Arimathaea 'an honourable counsellor, which also waited for the kingdom of God.'

clue_checks.clue: I was a disciple of Jesus, but secretly, for fear of the Jews.
clue_checks.reason: John 19:38 says Joseph was 'a disciple of Jesus, but secretly for fear of the Jews.'

clue_checks.clue: I went to Pilate and begged the body of Jesus.
clue_checks.reason: Mark 15:43 says he 'went in boldly unto Pilate, and craved the body of Jesus.' 'Begged' is the wording of Matthew 27:58 and Luke 23:52, so this is an acceptable paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: I laid Jesus in my own new tomb, hewn out in the rock.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 27:60, in context with verses 57-59 naming Joseph, says he 'laid it in his own new tomb, which he had hewn out in the rock.'

clue_checks.clue: I was a disciple living in Damascus.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 9:10 says there was a certain disciple at Damascus named Ananias. 'Living' is a fair paraphrase of 'at Damascus.'

clue_checks.clue: The Lord spoke to me in a vision about a man named Saul.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 9:10-12 records the Lord speaking to Ananias in a vision and telling him to enquire for one called Saul of Tarsus.

clue_checks.clue: I told the Lord I had heard how much evil Saul had done to the saints.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 9:13 quotes Ananias saying he had heard by many how much evil this man had done to the saints at Jerusalem.

clue_checks.clue: I put my hands on Saul so that he might receive his sight.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 9:17 says Ananias put his hands on Saul and said he was sent that Saul might receive his sight.

clue_checks.clue: I followed Jesus from the baptism of John until he was taken up.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 1:21-22 states this as Peter's qualification for the replacement apostle. It does not say it directly of Matthias, though his being put forward (1:23) implies he met it.

clue_checks.clue: My name was put forward together with Joseph called Barsabas.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 1:23 says they appointed two, Joseph called Barsabas and Matthias.

clue_checks.clue: The disciples prayed and gave forth their lots.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 1:24-26 records the prayer and that they gave forth their lots, and the lot fell on Matthias.

clue_checks.clue: I was numbered with the eleven apostles in the place of Judas.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 1:26 says he was numbered with the eleven. The phrase 'in the place of Judas' comes from the context in 1:25 (the apostleship from which Judas fell), not from 1:26 itself.

clue_checks.clue: I was a prisoner in Jerusalem.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 27:16 calls Barabbas a notable prisoner. The verse does not name Jerusalem, though the surrounding narrative of Pilate's judgment places him there.

clue_checks.clue: I had been bound with others who had made insurrection and committed murder.
clue_checks.reason: Mark 15:7 says Barabbas lay bound with them that had made insurrection with him, who had committed murder in the insurrection. The clue is a fair paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: Pilate offered the crowd a choice between Jesus and me.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 27:17 has Pilate asking whether to release Barabbas or Jesus which is called Christ.

clue_checks.clue: The people asked for me to be released.
clue_checks.reason: Mark 15:11 says the chief priests moved the people to have Pilate release Barabbas, which implies the people asked for him. This is consistent with Mark 15:8–15.

clue_checks.clue: I was a king who came to Caesarea with Bernice to greet Festus.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 25:13 says king Agrippa and Bernice came unto Caesarea to salute Festus.

clue_checks.clue: Festus told me about a prisoner named Paul.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 25:14 says Festus declared Paul's cause unto the king, a man left in bonds.

clue_checks.clue: Paul made his defence before me.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 26:1-2 has Paul answer for himself before king Agrippa. Paul also defended himself before Felix and Festus, but the earlier clues already single out Agrippa, so the full set is unique.

clue_checks.clue: I said to Paul, Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 26:28 quotes this verbatim as Agrippa's words.

clue_checks.clue: I was a young man in Troas.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 20:9 calls Eutychus 'a certain young man,' but it does not name Troas. The location comes from Acts 20:6, where they 'came unto them to Troas.' The clue is accurate, but the cited verse supports only part of it.

clue_checks.clue: I sat in a window while Paul preached until midnight.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 20:7 says Paul 'continued his speech until midnight,' and Acts 20:9 says Eutychus 'sat in a window.'

clue_checks.clue: I fell into a deep sleep and fell down from the third loft.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 20:9 says he was 'fallen into a deep sleep' and 'fell down from the third loft.'

clue_checks.clue: Paul embraced me, and I was brought alive.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 20:10 says Paul fell on him, 'embracing him,' and Acts 20:12 says 'they brought the young man alive.'

clue_checks.clue: I departed from my master for a season.
clue_checks.reason: Philemon 1:15 says he 'departed for a season.' The 'thou' addressed is Philemon, whom the context (v16, 'servant') shows was his master, so 'from my master' is a fair contextual paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: Paul begat me while he was in bonds.
clue_checks.reason: Philemon 1:10 names Onesimus, 'whom I have begotten in my bonds.'

clue_checks.clue: I was once unprofitable to my master, but now profitable.
clue_checks.reason: Philemon 1:11: 'in time past was to thee unprofitable, but now profitable.' 'Thee' is Philemon, his master.

clue_checks.clue: Paul sent me back to Philemon as a brother beloved.
clue_checks.reason: Philemon 1:12 has 'Whom I have sent again,' and 1:16 has 'not now as a servant, but above a servant, a brother beloved.'

clue_checks.clue: Many gathered to pray at my mother Mary's house in Jerusalem.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 12:12 names Mary as 'the mother of John, whose surname was Mark,' and says many were gathered there praying. Jerusalem is clear from the context of Peter's release.

clue_checks.clue: I went with Barnabas and Saul but left them in Pamphylia.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 15:38 confirms Mark departed from them from Pamphylia. However, 'him' is identified only through 15:37, and the verse does not itself say Mark travelled with Barnabas and Saul. Acts 12:25 and 13:5, 13 state that directly.

clue_checks.clue: Paul and Barnabas parted over whether to take me again.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 15:37-39 says Barnabas wanted to take John Mark, Paul refused, the contention was sharp, they separated, and Barnabas took Mark.

clue_checks.clue: Paul later wrote that I was profitable to him for the ministry.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Timothy 4:11 says 'Take Mark... for he is profitable to me for the ministry.'

clue_checks.clue: My father was a priest of Midian.
clue_checks.reason: Exodus 2:16 names the priest of Midian and his seven daughters but does not name Zipporah. Exodus 2:21 identifies her as one of those daughters, so the clue holds when read with the explanation.

clue_checks.clue: I met my husband when he helped my sisters and me water our flock.
clue_checks.reason: Exodus 2:17 shows Moses helping the daughters water their flock. That he became her husband, and that she was among them, comes from Exodus 2:21, not from this verse.

clue_checks.clue: God sent my husband to bring Israel out of Egypt.
clue_checks.reason: Exodus 3:10 has God sending Moses to bring Israel out of Egypt, and Moses is Zipporah's husband (Exodus 2:21).

clue_checks.clue: I circumcised my son with a sharp stone.
clue_checks.reason: Exodus 4:25 states this explicitly and names Zipporah.
